title_prefix: A tx record that fails to parse is skipp
mechanism: wallet-load-tx-records (src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp:1222-1242) has two failure arms for a tx row and both are pure warnings: a parse error pushes "Error reading wallet tx record: ~A" into the warnings list, and a stored-txid / recomputed-hash mismatch pushes "Wallet tx record hash mismatch; record skipped (rescan to recover)"; in both cases the record is dropped and the loop moves on. Nothing raises a rescan-required condition and no caller has a channel for one: wallet-attach-chain (src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp:1667-1722) takes only NODE and WALLET, always resolves the stored best-block locator's fork with find-fork-in-active-chain and rescans only from there, so the block that carried the lost transaction is never re-read. Core's LoadTxRecords turns exactly these two conditions into DBErrors::NEED_RESCAN -- LoadToWallet returns false when deserialization throws or wtx.GetHash() != hash (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/walletdb.cpp:1015-1030) -- CreateWalletFromFile sets rescan_required from it, keeps loading, and warns 'Error reading %s! Transaction data may be missing or incorrect. Rescanning wallet.' (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/wallet.cpp:3140-3142), and AttachChain then leaves rescan_height at 0 instead of using the stored locator, 'If rescan_required = true, rescan_height remains equal to 0' (wallet.cpp:3200-3211), so the whole chain is rescanned from the wallet birthday and the lost transaction is rebuilt. A second divergence sits above ours: load-wallets-on-startup (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1638-1671) calls %load-and-attach-wallet and DISCARDS its second value, so the warnings list -- the only trace this leaves -- exists on the loadwallet RPC reply and nowhere else.
consequence: The wallet loads and serves a balance and a history that are silently wrong, and it does not repair itself. Executed on regtest with a single mature 50 BTC coinbase and one byte of the single tx record's value flipped: before, mine.trusted 50.0 with 1 tx in mapWallet; after the reload, mine.trusted 0.0, txcount 0, listtransactions 0 entries, one warning string. Running the real next step, wallet-attach-chain, left it at 0.0; a full unload/reload/attach cycle -- a node restart -- left it at 0.0 with txcount 0. The only recovery is an operator noticing and running a rescan by hand: an explicit rescanblockchain 0 restored (:AFTER-EXPLICIT-RESCAN (:TRUSTED 50.0)) with txcount 1. That last step also shows the loss is recoverable data, not lost funds -- the coins are on chain and the descriptors are intact -- which is what holds this at S2 rather than S1. It is squarely S2 rather than S3 because the wrong number is a BALANCE an operator acts on: a zero balance on a wallet that holds coins invites the operator to conclude the coins are gone, or to re-derive and reuse addresses; and on the path most operators actually take, a bitcoind restart, there is no warning at all because load-wallets-on-startup drops the warnings. The control case (deleting the record outright) also yields 0.0 with NO warning, and Core behaves the same way there -- only the CORRUPT case diverges.
evidence: Probes under build/ga11v/p4-wallet-corrupt.lisp, run with scripts/dev.sh eval on the project container in worktree bl-ga11v-storage-s2, driving the shipped handlers (rpc-createwallet, rpc-getnewaddress, rpc-generatetoaddress, rpc-unloadwallet, load-wallet, wallet-attach-chain, rpc-getbalances, rpc-listtransactions, rpc-rescanblockchain) under with-wallet-chain-node. Corruption is done on the closed wallet LevelDB through wallet-db-open + leveldb-put :sync t, XORing #xFF into the middle byte of the one tx record's value (258-byte value, byte 129). (1) ga11v-p4 :flip -> (:BEFORE (:TRUSTED 50.0) :TXCOUNT-BEFORE 1 :WARNINGS ("Wallet tx record hash mismatch; record skipped (rescan to recover)") :AFTER-LOAD (:TRUSTED 0.0) :TXCOUNT-AFTER 0 :LISTTRANSACTIONS-AFTER 0 :ATTACH-CHAIN-ERROR NIL :AFTER-ATTACH (:TRUSTED 0.0) :ATTACH-CHAIN-ERROR-2 NIL :AFTER-RESTART (:TRUSTED 0.0) :TXCOUNT-AFTER-RESTART 0). (2) ga11v-p4 :delete control -> same 0.0 with :WARNINGS NIL. (3) ga11v-p4-rescan counter-probe -> (:RESCAN-RESULT (("start_height" . 0) ("stop_height" . 102)) :AFTER-EXPLICIT-RESCAN (:TRUSTED 50.0) :TXCOUNT-AFTER-RESCAN 1). Ours: src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp:1222-1242,1667-1722; src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1039-1120,1225-1262,1597-1635,1638-1671. Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/walletdb.cpp:1015-1030; refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/wallet.cpp:3140-3142,3200-3211.
fix_shape: Do not implement here. Carry Core's NEED_RESCAN signal, do not widen the warning. Give wallet-load-tx-records (and %load-wallet-records, which already threads WARNINGS) a second returned flag set on exactly Core's two conditions -- the record failed to parse, or its recomputed hash does not match the stored key -- and have load-wallet return it alongside the wallet and warnings, keeping the wallet loaded as Core does. %load-and-attach-wallet then passes it to wallet-attach-chain as a RESCAN-REQUIRED keyword whose only effect is to force rescan-height to 0 instead of consulting wallet-loaded-locator, which is literally Core's 'rescan_height remains equal to 0' branch; the existing birth-time gate, the prune refusal and the reserver stay exactly as they are, since Core runs the same rescan machinery from a different start height. Add Core's warning text alongside the current one, and -- separately from the Core port but in the same change, because it is what makes the divergence invisible on a restart -- have load-wallets-on-startup log the warnings it currently discards. A test should pin the whole path: fund a regtest wallet, unload, flip a byte in the tx record, load through %load-and-attach-wallet, and assert the balance is back without an explicit rescanblockchain, with the positive control that the same test reads 0.0 on the pre-fix code.
